item.title: Takarazuka Grand Theater: Japan's All-Female Revue — Guide
item.description: The Takarazuka Revue is one of the most singular institutions in Japanese theatre: founded in 1914 to draw passengers to a new railway line, it stages lavish musicals — European romances, historical epics, manga adaptations and glittering revue finales — performed entirely by women. Its five troupes are led by otokoyaku, actresses who specialise in male roles and command extraordinary devotion from a largely female audience. The 2,500-seat Grand Theater in Takarazuka is its home, and the whole town around it, with its rose-lined avenue and theatre shops, revolves around the company.
